scope: ARWP Image Discovery IDL-01 through IDL-08 applied to the canonical cognitive-bias page cohort and its unique editorial assets.

findings.evidence: Canonical bias pages expose ordinary img references to same-origin WebP assets; the final-artifact gate verifies the asset exists and the live gate verifies representative image responses are fetchable image content.

scripts/apply-image-discovery.mjs aligns og:image, twitter:image and WebPage.primaryImageOfPage to each canonical bias page's unique editorial asset; scripts/check-image-discovery.mjs verifies the final generated artifact.

The final sitemap receives the Google image namespace and one image:image/image:loc entry for every canonical bias page. Deprecated image:caption, image:geo_location, image:title and image:license fields are rejected.

Informative bias hero images keep non-empty contextual alt text, decorative catalogue thumbnails remain empty-alt, and data/image-metadata.json provides reviewed visual-specific descriptions without inventing unreviewed image details.

The existing max-image-preview:large policy is preserved; final and live Image Discovery checks reject unintended noimageindex on the canonical bias cohort while keeping publisher controls authoritative.

Canonical bias pages use unique page-relevant editorial art. Current markup declares 1024x768 display dimensions, but encoded pixel dimensions are not inferred from markup. Discover-specific 1200px guidance remains a separate optimization/watch and is not treated as a general image-indexing failure.

Current unique bias images use stable crawlable src URLs. Responsive variant generation is intentionally left as a later delivery/performance optimization rather than being represented as required for image indexing.

This rollout does not introduce per-image licensing or creator-display claims. The site licence remains governed by the existing publisher policy, and deprecated image-sitemap licensing fields are explicitly rejected.
